stimulus: Agricultural bulletin: Most of the orchards in the Calder Valley, a region long known for its fruit exports, are certified organic. Every certified-organic orchard, whatever its size or output, is inspected annually by the agricultural board. And under the reporting regulation the province adopted this spring, no orchard that the board inspects annually is exempt from the new pesticide-reporting rule, regardless of what it grows.
question_stem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the statements above?
choice_a: Most of the orchards in the Calder Valley are not inspected annually by the agricultural board.
choice_b: No orchard in the Calder Valley is exempt from the new pesticide-reporting rule.
choice_c: Most of the orchards in the Calder Valley are not exempt from the new pesticide-reporting rule.
choice_d: Most of the orchards that the agricultural board inspects annually are in the Calder Valley.
choice_e: Any orchard that is not inspected annually by the agricultural board is not in the Calder Valley.
prediction_text: Chain the quantifiers: most Valley orchards are organic; organic means inspected; inspected means not exempt. So most Valley orchards are not exempt.
trap_d: illicitly converts the direction of the chain
trap_e: treats most as all and contraposes
explanation_a: The statements support the opposite: the organic majority is inspected, so most Valley orchards are inspected.
explanation_b: Orchards outside the organic majority might be exempt; nothing rules that out, so the universal claim overreaches.
explanation_c: Correct. The organic majority is inspected, and inspected orchards are not exempt; so most Valley orchards are not exempt.
explanation_d: The premises say nothing about how many inspected orchards lie in the Valley; the chain does not convert.
explanation_e: Only most Valley orchards are organic, so an uninspected orchard could still be in the Valley.
